what: The score combines exact insertion distance with four candidate-level terms: a depot-distance saving credit, an adaptive large-demand credit, a capacity-compatible neighborhood continuation credit, and an unused-capacity penalty when the insertion would necessarily close the route. The slot-specific insertion delta chooses the position; the remaining terms determine customer priority. Runtime is O(len(current_route) + len(unassigned)) per call with O(1) extra space.
why: Farthest-customer route seeding benefits from a moderated savings-style radial term that keeps early construction in the seed's geographic region instead of immediately selecting cheap depot-adjacent insertions. The continuation term favors candidates connected to another customer that can still fit, encouraging coherent clusters that intra-route 2-opt can subsequently reorder. Demand urgency and tight-closure pressure address heterogeneous demands and routes near capacity, including instances containing customers that consume most of a vehicle. The coefficients are scale-normalized but heuristic rather than learned or guaranteed; the method can still make poor choices when the best packing requires nonlocal combinations, and its one-customer continuation statistic does not model full future routes.
